set.approach: The Bridge Group lies in the Menagerie Wilderness off Highway 20 near Santiam Pass. Take Moose Mountain Road (Road 2027) to forest roads 850 or 857 and then 856, and continue on foot as far as the road system allows. A trail drops from the end of the roads down to the Bridge Group formation, where the route is found.

review.notes: Route page only points to a guidebook; approach from the area pages. No descent stated.

set.approach: The Bridge Group lies in the Menagerie Wilderness off Highway 20 near Santiam Pass, reached by Moose Mountain Road (Road 2027), forest roads 850/857 and 856 and then a trail down to the formation. Electric Ladyland is on the underside of the Bridge formation and starts from the saddle beneath it, which has a two-bolt anchor. Either scramble to the saddle from the south base of the gully or rappel in from the top of the Bridge.

review.notes: Route page for the start; area page for road access. Top-out descent not stated.

set.approach: The Bridge Group lies in the Menagerie Wilderness off Highway 20 near Santiam Pass, reached by Moose Mountain Road (Road 2027), forest roads 850/857 and 856 and then a trail down to the formation. The Newt Route starts beside the large tree at the west end of the south leg of the bridge, on the uphill side.
set.descent_text: Cross back over the bridge from the summit and scramble down to the saddle on the uphill side.

review.notes: Route page states start and walk-off.

set.approach: Park at the Rooster Rock trailhead and take the steep trail up to Rooster Rock, going right at the fork. Below Rooster Rock, climbers' trails descend through scree to its base and on beneath Hen Rock. Chicken Rock is just west of Hen Rock and shows up on your right as you go beneath Hen. Rawhide starts on the northeast side, between the chicken and the hen, and traverses beneath Sticky Fingers and Free Bird.
set.descent_text: Chicken Rock is descended by a rappel from the top.

review.notes: Crag page states the rappel from the top; rope/height counts left out.

set.approach: Get onto the Black Lake Trail from Anthony Lake Campground or the Elkhorn Crest trailhead. A little past Lilypad Lake, take the gently rolling ski and bike trail south, then pick a path up the forested slope to the boulder field under Gunsight Dome. Gunsight Slab is directly above: work right along the edge of the trees, then bear left onto the ledge beneath the slab. Zig-Zag begins a few steps short of a single large fir in the middle of that ledge.
set.descent_text: There are two ways down. One is a single-rope rappel from a tree on climber's right, as low on the slab as can be reached. The other is a walk-off to climber's left along the summit rocks until they end at trees, then sharply left onto the ledges that lead back down to the foot of the climb; the top of that ledge must be found, since heading straight down through the forest ends at the base of the boulder field.

review.notes: Route page for descent options; slab and dome pages for approach.

set.approach: Park as for Britt Nichols Park, walk the spur road to its end and take the well-defined trail on the left downhill to the top of Scorpion Buttress. From the top of Scorpion Butte either rappel into West Gully or follow the steep switchbacking trail on the right to the middle of the gully. Gym Wall is on the left heading down, and the route begins in the gully above the tree on its right side; belay from the tree.

review.notes: Approach from route, Gym Wall, West Gully and Scorpion Buttress pages; no descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the Rooster Rock trailhead and take the steep trail up to Rooster Rock, going right at the fork. Below Rooster Rock, climbers' trails descend through scree to its base and on beneath Hen Rock. Hen Rock sits between Chicken Rock and Rooster Rock, and Winter Sunshine is on the right side of its south face.
set.descent_text: Descent is a rappel down the north face from rings at the top.

review.notes: Route page states the north-face rappel; length left out.

set.approach: From Anthony Lake follow the Hoffer Lakes Trail as far as the higher of the two Hoffer Lakes. The Lower Wall is in the small valley southwest of the lake: scramble around the slabs on the south side of the lake to a meadow, where the wall shows on the right side of the valley, and a faint trail leads to its base. Cammin' Away is the right-trending crack.
set.descent_text: The crag has no anchors suitable for rappelling. Tree anchors at the top of the crack can be cleaned, and a gully downhill and to the right of the wall gives a scramble down.

review.notes: Crag page states no rappel anchors and the gully scramble; route page states tree anchors.

set.approach: Follow the approach to West Gully and the Gym Wall, by the trail from the top of Scorpion Buttress or by rappelling in. At the bottom of the gully the Prayer Wall faces the Gym Wall. The small madrone tree hung with prayer flags marks the base, and it also marks the start of Madrone Crack.

review.notes: Approach from route and area pages; descent not tied to this route.

set.approach: Park at the Rooster Rock trailhead and take the steep trail up to Rooster Rock, going right at the fork. Below Rooster Rock, climbers' trails descend through scree to its base and on beneath Hen Rock. Rooster Rock is the first pinnacle reached off the trail. The route starts on the big flake at the foot of the north face.
set.descent_text: Rap rings at the top of the north face provide the way down.

review.notes: Route page states the rings at the top.

set.approach: From Anthony Lake follow the Hoffer Lakes Trail to the upper Hoffer Lake. The Upper and Lower Walls are in the little valley that runs southwest from the lake: scramble around the slabs on the south side to a meadow, then follow the faint trail past the Lower Wall and steeply on along the base of the escarpment to the Upper Wall. North Flake starts in a corner and follows the flake. The anchors are on the big ledge at the top, set well back from the edge.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; route page for the line. Descent not explicitly stated.

set.approach: From Anthony Lake follow the Hoffer Lakes Trail to the upper Hoffer Lake.
